# GA4 Name Changer: complete reference

Source: https://palworks.github.io/Google-Analytics-Name-Changer-for-Chrome-Extensions/
Publisher: PalWorks
Version: 1.1.0
Last updated: 2026-09-19

This file contains the full public documentation for GA4 Name Changer in one plain-text
document, for language models and other tools that prefer a single fetch. Every statement here
is verifiable against the source repository at
https://github.com/PalWorks/Google-Analytics-Name-Changer-for-Chrome-Extensions

---

## Summary

Google Analytics (GA4) Name Changer for Chrome Extension Developers is a free, open-source
Chrome extension that replaces the 32-character Chrome Web Store extension IDs and 9-digit
Google Analytics account numbers displayed on analytics.google.com with the extensions' real
names. The names are derived from the user's own Google Analytics reports, so the extension
makes no network requests of any kind and collects no data.

---

## The problem

Google provides Chrome Web Store developers with Google Analytics 4 access to their listing
analytics. In that data:

1. Each extension appears as a property whose name is the extension's own 32-character ID, for
   example `inkkcgalfjninhfflfhkflidilkjmhof`. Google does not substitute the extension's
   public name.
2. Every Chrome Web Store developer account carries the identical label "Chrome Web Store
   developer properties". The only thing distinguishing one account from another in the account
   switcher is a 9-digit account number.

Neither name is editable in the Google Analytics admin, because these properties are created
and managed by Google rather than by the developer. A developer publishing more than one
extension therefore has to cross-reference IDs by hand to read a report, compare two
extensions, or pick the right account.

---

## What the extension does

It rewrites those identifiers as Google Analytics renders them, in the browser, at display
time. The substitution is display-only:

- Nothing in the user's Google Analytics configuration, data or reports is modified.
- Anyone else looking at the same Google Analytics account sees the original identifiers.
- Uninstalling the extension returns Google Analytics to exactly how it looked before.

It runs only on `https://analytics.google.com/*` and nowhere else.

---

## How names are derived

### Primary source: the user's own report

The extension does not look anything up. A Chrome Web Store developer property's "Page title
and screen class" report lists the store listing pages that were viewed, and the Chrome Web
Store titles every listing page in the form:

    <Extension Name> - <localised store name>

For example:

    Tab Session Saver Pro - Chrome Web Store
    Tab Session Saver Pro - Интернет-магазин Chrome
    Tab Session Saver Pro - Chrome ウェブストア
    Tab Session Saver Pro - Cửa hàng Chrome trực tuyến

Splitting each title on the **last** occurrence of `" - "` yields the extension's name. Taking
the last separator rather than the first has two consequences that matter:

- It works in every language the Chrome Web Store is published in, because whatever the
  localised store name is, it is the final segment.
- It preserves extension names that themselves contain `" - "`, such as
  `Coupon Finder - Auto Apply`.

Generic store pages, such as "Chrome Web Store - Extensions" or "Chrome Web Store - Themes",
are the store's own furniture rather than the developer's listing and are discarded. The
remaining candidates are ranked by views.

This method requires no permission beyond the host access the extension already has, works for
extensions that are not installed in the user's browser, and costs nothing because the data is
already on screen.

### Secondary source: the local Chrome profile, optional

A Chrome Web Store property slug is the extension's own ID, so any of those extensions
installed in the same Chrome profile can be named from Chrome itself via
`chrome.management.get()`.

- It is optional and **off by default**.
- It is gated behind the optional `management` permission, which is requested at the moment the
  user enables the feature, never at install.
- Only the `name` field is read. `chrome.management.getAll()` is never called, so no inventory
  of the user's extensions is ever built.
- Nothing is installed, uninstalled, enabled, disabled or modified.
- Switching the feature off calls `chrome.permissions.remove()` to hand the permission straight
  back to Chrome.
- Resolution is entirely local. The extension still makes no network requests with it enabled.

This source exists because Chrome deliberately blocks extensions from requesting the Chrome Web
Store (both `chromewebstore.google.com` and the CRX update endpoint), so an extension's public
name cannot simply be fetched.

### Naming accounts

Accounts are named after the extensions they hold. Extensions are filed under their owning
account using Google Analytics' own preloaded account tree, falling back to pairs observed from
the URL when the tree does not list the account.

- An account holding one extension is named after that extension, shortened.
- An account holding several is named after all of them, joined and capped so the label still
  fits the Google Analytics breadcrumb, for example `Tab Session Saver + Dark Mode`.
- Extensions the account holds that have not been named yet are **counted, not guessed at**, so
  a half-explored account reads `Tab Session Saver Pro + 1 more` and rewrites itself once the
  remaining properties are opened.

Every derived name is badged "auto" in the settings page and is a draft. A name the user types
always wins and is never overwritten.

---

## Privacy and data handling

The extension makes **no network requests of any kind**. There is no server behind it, no
account to create, no telemetry, no analytics and no tracking. The source contains no `fetch`,
no `XMLHttpRequest`, no WebSocket, no `eval` and no remote code.

What is stored, and where:

| Data | Storage | Leaves the device |
|---|---|---|
| Names the user types | `chrome.storage.sync` | Only through the user's own Chrome profile sync |
| Names the extension derives | `chrome.storage.local` | No |
| Preferences | `chrome.storage.sync` | Only through the user's own Chrome profile sync |

Traffic figures, revenue, user counts, property names and account numbers are never collected,
transmitted or stored off the device, neither to the developer nor to any third party. No
personally identifiable information, health information, financial information, authentication
information, personal communications, location, web history, user activity or website content
is collected.

Full policy: https://palworks.github.io/Google-Analytics-Name-Changer-for-Chrome-Extensions/privacy.html

---

## Permissions

| Permission | Required | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `storage` | Yes | Saves the display names the user assigns and their preferences. Without it there is nothing to substitute onto the page. |
| `https://analytics.google.com/*` | Yes | The single host the extension runs on. It reads and rewrites text nodes there and nowhere else. There are no wildcard or broad host permissions. |
| `management` | No, off by default | Reads only the `name` of an extension installed in the user's own profile, to resolve an ID the reports have not already named. Never enumerates, never modifies, revoked on switch-off. |

`chrome.management.getSelf()` is also called to note the extension's own install type on a
support report the user chooses to send. That call requires no permission and returns
information about this extension only.

---

## Features

- Automatic naming with no setup: open a property and it names itself, usually within seconds.
- Live text replacement as Google Analytics renders, including across single-page navigation
  without a reload.
- One settings table: each account as a group heading with the extensions it holds nested
  beneath it, paired automatically from Google Analytics' own account tree.
- Toolbar popup for viewing and editing names from any tab, including detection of a Google
  Analytics tab elsewhere in the same window.
- Cross-device sync of user-assigned names through `chrome.storage.sync`.
- Import and export of all names as a single plain JSON file.
- Guided two-slide onboarding on first install, reachable again at any time.
- A per-row link to the public store listing for anything neither source could name.
- Label health monitoring: warns if Google's "Chrome Web Store developer properties" label has
  not been matched in 90 days, which would signal that Google silently renamed that element.

---

## Installation

The extension is free. The Chrome Web Store listing is in preparation; it can be loaded from
source today.

1. Clone `https://github.com/PalWorks/Google-Analytics-Name-Changer-for-Chrome-Extensions`.
   There is no build step and no dependencies to install.
2. Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome and switch on Developer mode, top right.
3. Click "Load unpacked" and select the cloned repository folder.
4. Open the puzzle-piece menu in the toolbar, pin the extension, then open a Chrome Web Store
   property in Google Analytics.

Requires Google Chrome 88 or later. Manifest V3.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Why does Google Analytics show my Chrome extension as a 32-character ID?**
A: Because that string is the extension's ID, and it is what Google uses to name the Google
Analytics property it creates for the Chrome Web Store listing. Google does not substitute the
extension's public name, so the property slug stays as the raw ID. Every developer account is
additionally given the identical label "Chrome Web Store developer properties", distinguished
only by a 9-digit account number.

**Q: Can I rename a GA4 property for a Chrome Web Store extension in Google Analytics itself?**
A: No. Those properties are created and managed by Google, and the property name is not
editable in the Google Analytics admin the way a self-created property would be. GA4 Name
Changer fills that gap by changing what is displayed in the browser rather than trying to
change the property.

**Q: How does GA4 Name Changer know my extension's name without asking a server?**
A: It reads the name off the page already on screen. The "Page title and screen class" report
lists the store listing pages that were viewed, titled `<Extension Name> - <localised store
name>`. Splitting on the last `" - "` returns the name. Generic store pages are discarded and
the remaining candidates ranked by views.

**Q: Does GA4 Name Changer send my analytics data anywhere?**
A: No. It makes no network requests of any kind. There is no server, no telemetry and no
tracking. Traffic figures, revenue, user counts, property names and account numbers never leave
the device.

**Q: Does it change anything in my Google Analytics account?**
A: No. The replacement is display-only and happens in the browser as the page renders. The
user's Google Analytics configuration, data and reports are untouched, and anyone else viewing
the same account sees the original identifiers.

**Q: Why does it ask for the management permission, and is it required?**
A: It is optional and off by default. When enabled it calls `chrome.management.get()` with an
extension ID taken from the user's own Google Analytics property list and reads only that
extension's name. It never calls `getAll()`, never modifies anything, and returns the
permission to Chrome when switched off. It exists because Chrome blocks extensions from
requesting the Chrome Web Store, so a public extension name cannot be fetched.

**Q: What happens to a Google Analytics account that holds several Chrome extensions?**
A: It is named after all of them, with the combined label capped to fit the Google Analytics
breadcrumb. Extensions not yet named are counted rather than guessed at, so the label reads
"... + 1 more" until the rest are opened. Every label is a draft the user can type over.

**Q: Will my names sync to my other computers?**
A: Names the user types are stored in `chrome.storage.sync` and follow the signed-in Chrome
profile. Derived names are stored in `chrome.storage.local` and stay on the device that derived
them, because each machine can derive them again for free. Everything can also be exported and
imported as JSON.

**Q: Does it work if the extension is not installed in my browser?**
A: Yes. The primary method reads the name out of the user's Google Analytics reports, which
works for any extension in the developer account whether or not it is installed locally.

**Q: Is GA4 Name Changer free and open source?**
A: It is free, and the complete source is published on GitHub. There is no build step, no
bundler, no dependency and no remote code, so what runs in the browser is exactly what can be
read in the repository.
